I'm looking forward to seeing what the Giants can do this year. After winning it all in '10, '12, and '14, maybe they can skip the leap year and do it twice in a row.

I'm interested to see how my Rays will do. We lost Friedman and Maddon, which most people would say was the core of our winning. Friedman, I'd argue, is actually a reason why we have such a depleted farm system. Back in 2011 or 2012, we had something like 11 picks in the first 75 overall picks and only like two of them have been anything good. That was our chance to reload and prepare for the future and we failed. What Friedman excelled at was getting the most for his trades, barring the Price trade (where I feel it was one player short of being a good trade). The hope is that Matt Silverman was the true mastermind and we can still succeed.

Joe Maddon, on the other hand, was all he was cracked up to be: kept the clubhouse loose, inventive, not afraid to take chances, methodical, etc.. It should be fun to watch him in the NL where strategy is much more important, but his greatest weakness was overthinking. The constantly changing lineup never allows any player to get settled into a spot. Some players may like that, some players may not benefit at all from it. The hope here is that Kevin Cash can continue the loose clubhouse feel and hopefully Longoria can help with that. He is the unquestioned leader in the clubhouse. We can also see if a stable lineup could help an offense that has certainly been lacking for the past few years.

Overall, I hope our pitching staff gets, and stays, healthy and can support this team to the playoffs. I don't want to get to optimistic, but I just can't help it on opening day! I think we can snag a wild card spot!
